papers.title: Identifying phase separation modulators mediated by the SARS-CoV-2 nucleocapsid protein using a structure-based drug discovery approach.
papers.abstract: As severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) continues to evolve through mutations and acquire resistance to existing antiviral agents, the persistence of post-pandemic infections remains a significant global health concern. To address these challenges, it is crucial to develop novel therapeutic agents that target previously unexplored viral or host mechanisms.
papers.summary: This study uses a structure-based drug discovery approach to identify small molecules that modulate phase separation driven by the SARS-CoV-2 nucleocapsid (N) protein, a mechanism not targeted by current antivirals. The work aims to uncover novel therapeutic candidates that could remain effective despite viral mutation and resistance to existing drugs.

papers.title: PROTAC-DB 4.0: an expanded knowledgebase of targeted protein degradation modalities with AI-powered knowledge discovery.
papers.abstract: Proteolysis-targeting chimeras (PROTACs) represent an emerging therapeutic modality that harnesses the ubiquitin-proteasome system to induce targeted protein degradation (TPD). Their event-driven and catalytic mechanisms provide new opportunities to target previously undruggable proteins. However, the rapid expansion of TPD technologies, including molecular glues (MGs) and X-functional targeting chimeras (XTACs), together with the increasing application of artificial intelligence (AI) in degrader design, highlights the need for comprehensive and continuously updated data resources. Here, we pr
papers.summary: PROTAC-DB 4.0 is an updated knowledgebase that expands coverage beyond classical PROTACs to include molecular glues and XTACs, reflecting the growing diversity of targeted protein degradation modalities. The resource also incorporates AI-powered knowledge discovery features to help researchers mine the accumulated degrader data. It serves as a centralized, continuously updated reference for designing and analyzing targeted protein degraders.

papers.title: The pharmacological potential and metabolic risks of Xiaojin Pill in sorafenib-resistant papillary thyroid carcinoma: an integrated network analysis.
papers.abstract: Sorafenib resistance limits the efficacy of treatments for advanced papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC). The antitumor potential of Xiaojin Pill (XJP) has been demonstrated, yet its mechanisms potentially implicated in sorafenib resistance and combinational toxicological risks remain unclear. This study aimed to examine the molecular mechanisms through which XJP may act on signaling pathways implicated in sorafenib resistance, and to assess its combinational toxicological risks during co-administration with sorafenib.
papers.summary: This study uses integrated network analysis to predict how Xiaojin Pill, a traditional Chinese medicine, might act on signaling pathways involved in sorafenib resistance in papillary thyroid carcinoma, and to assess toxicological risks when co-administered with sorafenib. The work is largely computational and predictive, identifying candidate mechanisms and potential combination risks rather than providing experimental validation.

papers.title: A broadly active flavivirus NS4B targeting compound that blocks NS4B-NS3 binding and replication organelle formation.
papers.abstract: Mosquito-borne orthoflaviviruses, including West Nile virus (WNV), dengue virus (DENV), Zika virus (ZIKV), and Japanese encephalitis virus (JEV), cause substantial global morbidity and mortality, yet no broadly effective direct-acting antivirals are available. The viral nonstructural protein NS4B has emerged as a promising antiviral target, although the compounds described to date are largely DENV-specific. Here we characterize SRI-38841, a xanthine analog derived from hit-to-lead optimization of a previously described WNV inhibitor, which inhibits WNV replication with an IC₉₀ of 0.87 µM and l
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors characterize SRI-38841, a xanthine analog optimized from a prior West Nile virus inhibitor, that inhibits WNV replication with an IC90 of 0.87 µM and shows broad activity against multiple mosquito-borne flaviviruses. The compound works by blocking the interaction between viral NS4B and NS3 proteins, which prevents formation of the replication organelle. This represents a promising pan-flavivirus antiviral strategy targeting a conserved viral protein interaction.

papers.title: GolgiFold: A Structural Predictome of Human Golgi Protein Complexes.
papers.abstract: The Golgi apparatus is a central hub for protein secretion and endolysosomal biogenesis, coordinating protein and vesicular trafficking pathways that maintain cellular homeostasis. Although hundreds of proteins associate with the Golgi, molecular assemblies have been defined for only a subset. Such well-characterized complexes have provided fundamental insights into Golgi trafficking, protein processing, and homeostasis, suggesting that systematic mapping of the broader Golgi interactome would uncover unrecognized components and regulatory mechanisms. Here, we systematically interrogate Golgi
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: GolgiFold presents a systematic structural predictome of human Golgi protein complexes, using computational structure prediction to map molecular assemblies across the Golgi interactome. Since only a subset of Golgi-associated proteins have well-defined complexes, this work aims to uncover unrecognized components and regulatory mechanisms governing Golgi trafficking, protein processing, and homeostasis. The resource provides structural hypotheses for many previously uncharacterized Golgi assemblies.

papers.title: Domain-Aware Enzyme Classification via Multiple Instance Learning.
papers.abstract: Accurate Enzyme Commission (EC) number prediction is fundamental to protein function annotation and metabolic pathway reconstruction. Recent methods based on protein language model embeddings or 3D structure have improved EC prediction, but important limitations remain. Whole-sequence embeddings can dilute local functional signals, such as catalytic residues and functional domains, whereas structure-based methods depend on accurate protein structures and are therefore difficult to apply broadly.
papers.summary: The paper introduces a domain-aware enzyme classification method that uses multiple instance learning to focus on local functional regions (e.g., catalytic residues and domains) rather than diluting signals across whole-sequence embeddings. This approach aims to improve Enzyme Commission number prediction without relying on accurate 3D structures, making it more broadly applicable than structure-based methods.

papers.title: ARIEL: an openly accessible database of experimental RNA-ligand binding affinities paired with 3D structures.
papers.abstract: RNA is an increasingly attractive target for small-molecule therapeutics, yet the rational design and computational modelling of RNA-binding small molecules are constrained by the scarcity of experimentally measured binding affinities linked to 3D structures. Here we present ARIEL (Affinity Resource for Interactions of RNA and Ligands), an openly accessible, manually curated database that pairs experimentally determined dissociation constants (Kd) of RNA-ligand complexes with the corresponding experimental structures. We screened 6954 RNA-containing structures from the Protein Data Bank, extra
papers.summary: ARIEL is a new manually curated database that links experimentally measured RNA-ligand binding affinities (Kd values) to their corresponding 3D structures, addressing a major bottleneck in RNA-targeted drug design. The authors screened nearly 7,000 RNA-containing structures from the Protein Data Bank to build this resource, which is openly accessible to the research community. This fills a critical gap for computational modeling and rational design of small molecules that bind RNA.

papers.title: Structural clustering across the tree of life reveals candidate Asgard-eukaryote homologs and a shared expansion of solenoids.
papers.abstract: Asgard archaea are the closest known prokaryotic relatives of eukaryotes, and their genomes encode many eukaryotic signature proteins (ESPs), homologs of proteins associated with eukaryotic cellular complexity. Because deep divergence limits sequence-based homology detection, structure-based searches are increasingly used to expand the ESP repertoire, but they start from individual Asgard proteins rather than the families those proteins belong to. Here we took a complementary, family-level approach, profiling the taxonomic composition of 1.89 million structural clusters from the AFESM database
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors performed a family-level structural clustering of 1.89 million protein structures from the AFESM database to trace how protein families are distributed across the tree of life. This approach identified candidate Asgard archaeal homologs of eukaryotic proteins and revealed a shared expansion of solenoid protein families in both Asgard archaea and eukaryotes. The work complements sequence-based homology searches by using structure to detect deeply divergent relationships.

papers.title: Simulating Directed Evolution In Silico with an Iterative, Physics-Based Workflow.
papers.abstract: Directed evolution consistently delivers engineered enzymes that facilitate diverse biocatalytic transformations. Despite advances in automation and high-throughput workflows, our ability to rapidly engineer novel enzymes is limited by our inability to thoroughly sample the vast protein design space. Generative artificial intelligence (AI) methods have alleviated this challenge to some degree, due to their ability to propose mutations based on learned patterns from complex protein data sets. However, the hidden logic of these AI-based methods can complicate our ability to reveal and exploit fu
papers.summary: This paper presents an iterative, physics-based computational workflow that simulates directed evolution in silico to engineer enzymes without relying on black-box AI models. The approach aims to overcome the limited sampling of protein design space by combining physics-based scoring with iterative mutation cycles, offering a more interpretable alternative to generative AI methods. The work addresses the challenge of rapidly engineering novel enzymes by providing a transparent, simulation-driven strategy for exploring sequence-function landscapes.

papers.title: Discovery and Design of YTHDF2-Selective and Pan-YTHDF Inhibitors for m6A Binding by the YTH Aromatic Cage.
papers.abstract: Recognition of N6-methyl-adenosine (m6A) in the RNA sequences by the YT521-B homology domain-containing protein family paralogs 1-3 (YTHDF1-3) is a dominant layer of myriad cellular regulation. Dysregulated YTHDF paralog expression and activities have been reported in cancer, including glioblastoma multiforme (GBM) in which YTHDF2 has been identified as a druggable dependency. Guided by structure-based in silico screening, we identified structurally related small-molecule compound families of promising YTHDF inhibitor compounds. Following in vitro screening, two hits, DT11 and DT15, emerged an
papers.summary: The authors used structure-based virtual screening to identify small-molecule inhibitors that bind the m6A-recognition aromatic cage of YTHDF proteins, yielding two hit compounds (DT11 and DT15) with promising in vitro activity. These compounds include both YTHDF2-selective and pan-YTHDF inhibitors, providing chemical probes to dissect paralog-specific m6A reader functions and potential leads for cancers such as glioblastoma where YTHDF2 is a druggable dependency.

papers.title: In-silico transcriptomic characterization analysis identifies SMAD5, USP2, and CUL4A as key biomarkers and therapeutic targets in colorectal cancer.
papers.abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is a molecularly heterogeneous malignancy requiring reproducible biomarkers and structurally tractable therapeutic targets. We applied an integrated transcriptomic, network, virtual-screening, docking, ADMET, and molecular-dynamics (MD) workflow using GSE8671, GSE14333, and GSE89076. Differential expression analysis (adjusted p < 0.05, |log2FC= ≥ 1) identified 2092 upregulated/9130 downregulated genes in GSE8671, 926/945 in GSE14333, and 2317/1456 in GSE89076. Cross-dataset concordance was highest between GSE8671 and GSE89076 (r = 0.70), with 1040 shared upregulated and
papers.summary: This study integrates transcriptomic datasets from three colorectal cancer cohorts with network analysis, virtual screening, docking, ADMET, and molecular dynamics to identify SMAD5, USP2, and CUL4A as candidate biomarkers and druggable targets. The workflow prioritizes these genes through cross-dataset differential expression concordance and structural tractability, nominating them for further experimental validation. The findings are computational predictions rather than experimentally confirmed biomarkers.

papers.title: Development of CYP8B1-specific inhibitors for metabolic diseases.
papers.abstract: Changes in bile acids (BAs) balance lead to various metabolic diseases, yet current treatment options targeting these changes remain severely limited. CYP8B1 (cytochrome P450, family 8, subfamily B, polypeptide 1) is a liver-exclusive enzyme that controls the synthesis of 12α-hydroxylated (12α-OH) BAs. Inhibiting CYP8B1 is an attractive therapeutic strategy for attenuating 12α-OH BA levels, remodeling the gut microbiota and thereby ameliorating metabolic diseases. CYP8B1-specific inhibitors are currently lacking due to structural similarities between the active site of CYP8B1 and other CYPs, a
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors report the development of CYP8B1-specific inhibitors, targeting a liver-exclusive enzyme that controls production of 12α-hydroxylated bile acids. Inhibiting this enzyme is proposed as a therapeutic strategy to remodel bile acid pools and the gut microbiota for treating metabolic diseases, addressing a gap caused by the structural similarity of CYP8B1's active site to other cytochrome P450 enzymes.

papers.title: Distance-AF Multimer: A Multi-Step Approach for Protein Complex Structure Modeling with User-Defined Distance Constraints.
papers.abstract: The three-dimensional structure of proteins provides essential insight into the molecular mechanisms underlying their function. Many biological activities are mediated through protein interactions, making accurate structural determination of protein complexes important. Despite significant advances in computational protein structure prediction, there are still many cases where protein complexes are not correctly assembled. In particular, there are cases where experimental data, such as distances between residue pairs in interacting proteins are available, yet existing prediction methods fail t
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Distance-AF Multimer is a new computational pipeline that improves protein complex structure prediction by incorporating user-defined distance constraints, such as those from crosslinking or other experimental data. It addresses cases where standard methods like AlphaFold-Multimer fail to assemble complexes correctly despite available distance information. The tool provides a multi-step workflow to guide structure modeling with these constraints.

papers.title: Free-Energy and Molecular Dynamics Analysis of Ser195 and Thr195 Rotameric States in Thrombin.
papers.abstract: Ser195 is highly conserved as the catalytic nucleophile in trypsin-like serine proteases, yet the molecular basis for the strong preference for serine over the chemically similar threonine residue remains unclear. Here, we used well-tempered metadynamics and microsecond-long molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to characterize the conformational energetics of S195 and T195 in thrombin. Well-tempered metadynamics revealed distinct rotameric free-energy landscapes in both the apo and the ligand-bound systems. In the apo state, S195 preferentially occupied a lower-angle rotameric state, while T195
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This study uses well-tempered metadynamics and microsecond-scale molecular dynamics simulations to compare the conformational free-energy landscapes of Ser195 and Thr195 in thrombin, addressing why serine is strongly preferred over threonine at this catalytic position in trypsin-like serine proteases. The simulations reveal distinct rotameric preferences between the two residues in both apo and ligand-bound states, with S195 favoring a lower-angle rotamer in the apo state. These findings offer a molecular-level explanation for the evolutionary conservation of serine at the catalytic nucleophile position.

papers.title: Edge-Aware Graph Attention Networks for Interpreting Biophysical Mechanisms from Molecular Dynamics Simulations.
papers.abstract: Graph attention networks (GATs) are emerging as powerful aritficial intelligence (AI) tools for learning biomolecular dynamics, yet extracting mechanistic insight from learned attention remains challenging. Here, we present an interpretable AI approach that combines molecular dynamics prediction with mechanistic interpretation through attention-derived communication networks. We develop three edge-aware GAT models - Edge-Conditioned, Edge-Injected, and Edge-Gated - that differ in how edge information is incorporated during message passing. Relative to a standard GAT, our edge-aware models impr
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint introduces three edge-aware graph attention network architectures (Edge-Conditioned, Edge-Injected, Edge-Gated) for learning biomolecular dynamics from molecular dynamics simulations, differing in how edge features are incorporated during message passing. The authors show these models outperform a standard GAT and, importantly, use the learned attention weights to derive communication networks that offer mechanistic biophysical interpretation. The work bridges predictive AI with interpretability for molecular dynamics.

papers.title: Structural Basis for Angiotensin II Type I Receptor G Protein-biased Signaling.
papers.abstract: Biased agonism at the angiotensin II type 1 receptor (AT1R) offers a promising strategy for developing safer cardiovascular therapeutics. While β-arrestin-biased agonism has been extensively investigated, G protein-biased signaling remains poorly understood. Here, we report structures of AT1R coupled to G protein and either the endogenous agonist angiotensin II (AngII) or the G protein-biased agonist TRV055. The ligands adopt similar overall poses, with coordinated rearrangements extending from the orthosteric pocket to the intracellular surface. The structures provide a detailed view of a TM7
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This study presents cryo-EM structures of the angiotensin II type 1 receptor (AT1R) bound to G protein with either the natural agonist angiotensin II or the G protein-biased agonist TRV055. The ligands adopt similar poses, but coordinated structural rearrangements propagate from the ligand-binding pocket to the intracellular surface, revealing how biased agonism is achieved at the receptor level. These structures provide a template for designing safer cardiovascular drugs that preferentially activate G protein signaling.

papers.title: AT1R-Selective Negative Allosteric Modulator Targeting the Epitope for Pathogenic Autoantibody Activation.
papers.abstract: A major therapeutic strategy for managing cardiovascular and renal diseases is the use of angiotensin receptor blockers (ARBs). These drugs block both pathogenic and physiological signaling by the angiotensin II type 1 receptor (AT1R) by preventing angiotensin II (AngII) binding to orthosteric pocket in transmembrane portion of AT1R. However, in many autoimmune diseases, AT1R activation is chronically driven by pathogenic autoantibody binding to a distinct extracellular surface located allosteric site. Currently, there are no allosteric inhibitors of AT1R available to mechanistically prevent t
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint describes the development of a selective negative allosteric modulator (NAM) for the angiotensin II type 1 receptor (AT1R) that targets the extracellular epitope recognized by pathogenic autoantibodies. Unlike conventional ARBs that block the orthosteric AngII binding site and thus inhibit both pathological and physiological signaling, this NAM aims to selectively block autoantibody-driven AT1R activation while preserving normal AngII signaling. The work addresses an unmet need in autoimmune diseases where AT1R is chronically activated by autoantibodies.

papers.title: A computational-experimental strategy identifies K-7174 against African swine fever.
papers.abstract: African swine fever (ASF), caused by the African swine fever virus (ASFV), poses a catastrophic threat to global swine production due to the absence of effective vaccines or therapeutics. Targeting the virally encoded RNA polymerase (RNAP), which is essential for viral transcription, offers a promising antiviral strategy. Capitalizing on our previously resolved high-resolution structure of ASFV RNAP, we conducted a rigorous structure-based virtual screening of two compound libraries (T001 and LF1000) to identify selective inhibitors. From 100 candidates validated in vitro, nine compounds ident
papers.summary: The authors used the high-resolution structure of the African swine fever virus RNA polymerase to perform structure-based virtual screening of two compound libraries, identifying K-7174 as a selective inhibitor of the viral enzyme. This computational-experimental pipeline yielded a promising antiviral candidate against African swine fever, a disease with no current vaccines or therapeutics.

papers.title: Structure-based prediction reveals FAM105A as an African swine fever virus I215L interactor.
papers.abstract: African swine fever virus (ASFV) causes a fatal hemorrhagic disease in pigs, leading to severe economic losses worldwide. The viral ubiquitin-conjugating enzyme I215L (E2) is critical for ASFV replication and modulation of host antiviral responses. Host deubiquitinating enzymes (DUBs) bind to E2 enzymes to inhibit the transfer of ubiquitin. In this study, we systematically screened 34 swine DUBs using HDOCK docking and AlphaFold3 modeling, identifying FAM105A as the most probable interactor. Co-immunoprecipitation assay validated the interaction between I215L and FAM105A. Structural analyses r
papers.summary: The authors used HDOCK docking and AlphaFold3 modeling to screen 34 swine deubiquitinating enzymes for interaction with the ASFV ubiquitin-conjugating enzyme I215L, identifying FAM105A as the top candidate. Co-immunoprecipitation experiments confirmed the I215L–FAM105A interaction, and structural analyses characterized the binding interface. This provides a structure-based pipeline for predicting viral-host protein interactions and nominates a new host factor in ASFV biology.

papers.title: HelixWings enables AI-driven enzyme engineering for biomimetic cofactor utilization.
papers.abstract: Biomimetic nicotinamide cofactors, such as nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMNH), can substantially reduce synthesis costs compared with natural cofactors like nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide phosphate (NADPH). However, natural enzymes generally exhibit poor activity with these alternative cofactors. Existing engineering approaches, including directed evolution and rational design, remain limited by experimental uncertainty or computational complexity. Here, we developed HelixWings, an artificial intelligence (AI)-driven screening platform that integrates conformational dynamics analysis with s
papers.summary: The authors present HelixWings, an AI-driven screening platform that combines conformational dynamics analysis with sequence-based prediction to engineer enzymes that can use biomimetic cofactors like NMNH instead of costly natural cofactors such as NADPH. This addresses the poor activity of natural enzymes with alternative cofactors, offering a more efficient alternative to directed evolution and rational design for reducing synthesis costs in biocatalysis.

papers.title: Integrating noncanonical amino acids and synthetic cofactors for the development of artificial metalloenzymes.
papers.abstract: Natural metalloenzymes harness the sophisticated synergy between canonical amino acids and metal cofactors to catalyze life-sustaining reactions. However, the limited chemical diversity of the twenty standard amino acids often restricts non-natural transformations. To overcome these constraints, artificial metalloenzymes (ArMs) integrate synthetic cofactors into protein scaffolds to enable unnatural catalytic functions. This review highlights how noncanonical amino acids (ncAAs) bridge the gap between natural enzyme architecture and synthetic chemistry. We examine genetic code expansion and co
papers.summary: This review discusses how artificial metalloenzymes (ArMs) combine synthetic metal cofactors with protein scaffolds to enable non-natural catalytic reactions. It focuses on how noncanonical amino acids (ncAAs), incorporated via genetic code expansion, can bridge natural enzyme architecture and synthetic chemistry, expanding the chemical diversity beyond the 20 standard amino acids.

papers.title: Acetyl tributyl citrate induces neuronal ferroptosis through ATM-associated disruption of iron and redox homeostasis.
papers.abstract: Acetyl tributyl citrate (ATBC) is widely used as a non-phthalate plasticizer, raising concerns about its potential health effects. Although emerging evidence suggests that ATBC may adversely affect the nervous system, the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. Given the critical role of ferroptosis in neuronal injury, this study investigated whether ferroptosis contributes to ATBC-induced neuronal injury and explored the potential involvement of ataxia-telangiectasia mutated (ATM) in this process.
papers.summary: This study investigates whether acetyl tributyl citrate (ATBC), a common non-phthalate plasticizer, causes neuronal damage through ferroptosis, an iron-dependent form of cell death. The authors examine the role of the ATM protein in linking ATBC exposure to disrupted iron and redox homeostasis, suggesting a mechanistic pathway for ATBC neurotoxicity.

papers.title: Anticancer activity of sodium propionate in hepatocellular carcinoma cells via downregulation of HDAC2 and HDAC6.
papers.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is an aggressive malignancy driven by epigenetic dysregulation. This study investigates the anticancer potential of sodium propionate (SP) as an epigenetic modulator targeting histone deacetylases (HDACs) using an integrated in silico and in vitro approach. Bioinformatics analyses were conducted using publicly available HCC transcriptomic datasets from GEO database, disease gene database (GeneCards database), and chemical-gene interaction networks (Comparative Toxicogenomic Database) to identify potential therapeutic targets, HDAC2 and HDAC6 as key therapeutic ta
papers.summary: This study combines bioinformatics analysis of public HCC transcriptomic and chemical-gene interaction datasets with in vitro experiments to show that sodium propionate, a short-chain fatty acid, exerts anticancer effects on hepatocellular carcinoma cells by downregulating the histone deacetylases HDAC2 and HDAC6. The work identifies these HDACs as key therapeutic targets and positions sodium propionate as a potential epigenetic modulator for HCC treatment.

papers.title: From prediction to creation: How AI-driven design is reshaping microbial biocatalysis.
papers.abstract: Enzyme engineering has long relied on rational design and directed evolution, yet both remain bounded by natural enzyme space - a constraint felt acutely across the largely uncharacterised microbial world. The 2021 advent of accurate structure prediction marked an inflection point, catalysing AI methods that now extend far beyond folding. These tools are organism-agnostic; the microbial domain is their proving ground because it supplies both the uncharacterised sequence space and the expression hosts. Here we examine three stages: mining microbial sequence space; generative design, whether con
papers.summary: This review argues that AI has moved enzyme engineering beyond predicting protein structures to actually creating new enzymes, especially from the vast, largely uncharacterized microbial sequence space. It traces three stages—mining microbial sequences, generative design of novel biocatalysts, and the broader shift from prediction to creation—and highlights microbes as both the source of unexplored sequence diversity and the hosts for expressing designed enzymes.

papers.title: BioLiP3: a protein-ligand affinity database integrating curated data with LLM-enabled literature mining.
papers.abstract: Quantitative binding affinities and three-dimensional protein-ligand structures provide complementary information essential for structure-based drug discovery, yet these data remain largely disconnected across existing databases and the biomedical literature. We present BioLiP3, a major extension of BioLiP that expands quantitative affinity coverage 13-fold within its structure-centered framework for biologically relevant interactions. BioLiP3 contains 593 423 affinity records, of which 591 820 are linked to three-dimensional protein-ligand structures: 45 386 experimentally resolved PDB comple
papers.summary: BioLiP3 is a major expansion of the BioLiP database that links quantitative protein-ligand binding affinities to three-dimensional structures, growing affinity coverage 13-fold to nearly 600,000 records. It integrates curated experimental data with LLM-enabled literature mining to connect binding measurements to PDB structures, addressing the disconnect between affinity data and structural data in existing resources. This provides a unified resource for structure-based drug discovery.

papers.title: NADPH-specific meso-diaminopimelate dehydrogenase from the archaeon Pyrococcus sp. stereoselectively aminates α-keto acids using NADH.
papers.abstract: Enzymatic asymmetric D-amination of carbonyl compounds and keto acids is of great interest in biotechnology. Stable D-stereoselective NAD-dependent dehydrogenases are required for the synthesis of D-amino acids from α-keto acids, because they can use ammonium ion as the amino group donor and allow high product yield via coenzyme recycling. However, these enzymes are rare in nature. Here, we describe the first archaeal meso-diaminopimelate dehydrogenase from Pyrococcus sp. (PyrDAPDH). The enzyme is active with either NADP(H) or NAD(H) and catalyzes reductive amination of various α-keto acids an
papers.summary: Researchers characterized the first meso-diaminopimelate dehydrogenase from an archaeon (Pyrococcus sp.), showing it can use either NADH or NADPH to stereoselectively aminate α-keto acids into D-amino acids. This expands the limited toolkit of stable, D-stereoselective dehydrogenases useful for biocatalytic production of D-amino acids with coenzyme recycling.

papers.title: Identification of small-molecule inhibitors of the SARS-CoV-2 RBD-ACE2 interaction by structure- and affinity-based screening.
papers.abstract: The receptor-binding domain (RBD) of the severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) spike protein mediates viral entry through its interaction with angiotensin-converting enzyme 2 (ACE2), making it an attractive target for antiviral intervention. However, the broad and relatively shallow ACE2-binding interface presents a challenge for small-molecule inhibitor discovery. In this study, we explored conserved regions outside the ACE2-binding interface as potential druggable sites for small-molecule inhibitors targeting the SARS-CoV-2 RBD. Structure-based virtual screening was pe
papers.summary: The authors used structure-based virtual screening and affinity-based methods to search for small-molecule inhibitors of the SARS-CoV-2 spike RBD–ACE2 interaction, focusing on conserved regions outside the shallow ACE2-binding interface as alternative druggable pockets. This work identifies candidate compounds targeting the RBD and suggests that allosteric or non-interface sites may be viable for small-molecule antiviral development.

papers.title: Toward the Rational Design of Tailored Ligands for Intrinsically Disordered Proteins through NMR.
papers.abstract: Understanding the driving forces governing the interactions between intrinsically disordered proteins and their potential ligands represents a key step toward the rational design of drugs targeting this type of proteins. Nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy provides a unique opportunity to achieve detailed atom-resolved information toward this ambitious goal. We present here a set of differently functionalized calix[4]arene-based multivalent ligands designed to target different regions of the well-characterized intrinsically disordered protein α-synuclein. Dedicated NMR experiments extended
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.summary: This paper describes a set of calix[4]arene-based multivalent ligands designed to bind different regions of the intrinsically disordered protein α-synuclein, using NMR to map interactions at atom-level resolution. The work aims to establish how ligand interactions with disordered proteins can be characterized and rationally optimized, a key step toward drug design for this challenging target class.

papers.title: From molecular pathways to nanocarrier design: a translational framework for lipid-based nanoparticles in Alzheimer's disease.
papers.abstract: Alzheimer's disease, being a complicated neurodegenerative disoder affects cognitive as well as memory functions. Characterised by amyloid-β aggregation, along with tau hyperphosphorylation, and cholinergic dysfunction, this disease is also associated with oxidative stress and neuroinflammation. Conventional clinical interventions, like acetylcholinesterase inhibitors and novel monoclonal antibodies predominantly rely on symptomatic alleviation of symptoms. Nevertheless, these conventional treatments come across considerable constraints, like temporary effectiveness, lesser therapeutic reach d
papers.summary: This review proposes a translational framework linking Alzheimer's disease molecular pathways—amyloid-β aggregation, tau hyperphosphorylation, cholinergic dysfunction, oxidative stress, and neuroinflammation—to the rational design of lipid-based nanocarriers for drug delivery. It argues that conventional treatments such as acetylcholinesterase inhibitors and monoclonal antibodies offer only symptomatic, limited benefit, and that nanocarrier engineering can improve therapeutic reach and efficacy by targeting these pathways.

papers.title: Cross-Linking Simulation at Metal Oxide-Thermoset Interfaces Using Quantum Chemical and Molecular Dynamics Methods.
papers.abstract: Understanding how oxidized metal surfaces catalyze the curing of epoxy resins is essential in improving the reliabilities of epoxy-metal oxide interfaces in multimaterial systems. The catalytic effects of hydroxylated oxidized tin metal (SnO2) surfaces on the cross-linking of epoxy resins were investigated using a hybrid approach that combined quantum chemical calculations with molecular dynamics simulations, wherein the reaction kinetics were modeled using Monte Carlo techniques. Analyzing the reaction pathways and spatial distributions at different hydroxylation levels revealed that fully hy
papers.summary: This study uses quantum chemical calculations combined with molecular dynamics and Monte Carlo reaction modeling to investigate how hydroxylated tin oxide (SnO2) surfaces catalyze epoxy resin cross-linking. The authors show that the degree of surface hydroxylation alters reaction pathways and the spatial distribution of cross-links at the metal oxide–thermoset interface. The work provides mechanistic insight into interfacial curing that could inform the design of more reliable epoxy–metal oxide joints in multimaterial systems.

papers.title: Cytoplasmic Expression of Papain Isozymes in Engineered Escherichia coli for Substrate Selectivity and Computational Insights.
papers.abstract: Challenges in isolating individual papain isozymes from papaya latex and in producing full-length, correctly folded, and soluble recombinant papain isozymes in Escherichia coli have limited detailed investigations into their distinct enzymatic properties and substrate specificities. In this study, we report the successful high-yield cytoplasmic expression of papain, protease omega, proteinase IV (pro-IV), and chymopapains I, II, and III in engineered E. coli SHuffle strains and a comprehensive investigation of their distinct biochemical and computational mechanistic insights. Building upon our
papers.summary: The authors achieved high-yield cytoplasmic expression of six papain-family isozymes (papain, protease omega, proteinase IV, and chymopapains I–III) in engineered E. coli SHuffle strains, overcoming prior difficulties in producing soluble, correctly folded recombinant plant proteases. They then characterized the distinct biochemical properties and substrate selectivities of each isozyme and complemented this with computational mechanistic analysis. The work provides a platform for studying individual papain isozymes that are hard to isolate from papaya latex.

papers.title: Poké: Fast and Reliable Neural-Network-Based Identification of Protein Ligandable Sites.
papers.abstract: Accurate identification of ligandable pockets is of key relevance for structure-based drug design; however, their identification remains challenging, particularly for cryptic sites that become accessible only upon conformational changes. Here, we introduce Poké, a high-performance pocket scouting tool that combines energetic mapping with a neural-network-based ligandability score, enabling rapid and reliable binding site detection in both static structures and long-timescale molecular dynamics (MD) trajectories. Poké identifies low-energy regions on protein surfaces through probe-based grid en
papers.summary: Poké is a new computational tool that identifies ligandable pockets on protein surfaces by combining energetic mapping with a neural-network-based ligandability score. It works on both static protein structures and long-timescale molecular dynamics trajectories, and is designed to detect cryptic sites that only appear upon conformational changes. The tool aims to make pocket detection faster and more reliable for structure-based drug design.

papers.title: Weighted Views Representation with Multi-Head Coulomb Attention for Molecular Property Prediction.
papers.abstract: We extend the weighted-views molecular featurization framework (d'Avezac, Botts, Mohlenkamp, and Zunger, 2011) by enriching it with single-atom properties and Coulomb pair information. We use these enriched views within a machine-learning architecture incorporating shared Transformers whose attention scores directly incorporate Coulomb interactions, weighted aggregation of view outputs, and a final prediction neural network. We demonstrate performance competitive with the state-of-the-art on the QM7 atomization energy benchmark (regression), ranking enantiomers by their docking scores (trained
papers.summary: The authors extend a weighted-views molecular featurization framework by adding single-atom properties and Coulomb pair information, then feed these enriched views into a Transformer architecture whose attention scores directly incorporate Coulomb interactions. They show competitive performance on the QM7 atomization energy regression benchmark and on ranking enantiomers by docking score.

papers.title: OPC3/LEW: A New Flexible Three-Site Water Model to Simulate Low-Electrostatic Environments.
papers.abstract: One of the main goals of computational simulations is to closely reproduce the environmental conditions in which biomolecules perform their physiological functions. However, the choice of water model is often based more on computational cost than on its effect on the molecular environment, as is the case with membrane proteins. These systems fulfill their biological function in low-polarity molecular environments that the most common or currently available water models do not reproduce accurately. In this work, we present a new flexible water model with three interaction sites that accurately
papers.summary: The authors introduce OPC3/LEW, a new flexible three-site water model designed to better reproduce low-electrostatic (low-polarity) environments, such as those experienced by membrane proteins. The model aims to address the tendency of standard water models to misrepresent these environments, where computational cost often drives model choice rather than accuracy. This offers a potentially improved option for simulations of biomolecules in low-polarity conditions.

papers.title: Machine Learning Prediction of Transport Properties in Amorphous Polymer Electrolytes Using Chemically Informed Structural Descriptors.
papers.abstract: Amorphous polymer electrolytes are promising candidates for next-generation lithium batteries. They offer improved safety and mechanical stability compared to conventional liquid electrolytes. However, predicting their transport performance remains challenging. Ionic conductivity and diffusivity depend on complex, coupled interactions between polymer structure, chemistry, and ion dynamics. This work leverages machine learning to predict four key transport properties in amorphous polymer electrolytes using a molecular dynamics data set of more than 6,000 polymer electrolyte systems. These are i
papers.summary: This study trains machine learning models on molecular dynamics data from over 6,000 amorphous polymer electrolyte systems to predict four key transport properties, including ionic conductivity and diffusivity. The models use chemically informed structural descriptors to capture the complex coupling between polymer chemistry, structure, and ion dynamics. The approach offers a faster alternative to expensive simulations for screening battery electrolyte candidates.

papers.title: AOXP: An Integrated Framework for Antioxidant Peptide Prediction Leveraging LLM-Based Semantic Features and Optimized Physicochemical Ensembles.
papers.abstract: Oxidative stress is a critical driver of various severe diseases, positioning antioxidant peptides (APs) as promising therapeutic agents. However, their discovery is constrained by the limitations of low-throughput wet-lab assays and insufficient computational prediction tools. To address this, we developed Antioxidant Peptides eXplorer (AOXP), a deep learning framework that leverages multiscale feature integration for high-precision AP prediction. Unlike existing models that often rely on isolated sequence patterns or manual feature descriptors, AOXP employs a hybrid encoding strategy that sy
papers.summary: AOXP is a deep learning framework for predicting antioxidant peptides that combines LLM-derived semantic sequence features with optimized physicochemical descriptors in a hybrid encoding strategy. This multiscale feature integration aims to overcome the limitations of prior models that rely on isolated sequence patterns or hand-crafted descriptors, offering higher-precision computational screening of therapeutic peptides.

papers.title: Structural basis for saccharide binding by human RNase 2/EDN: Insights into its potential lectin-like properties.
papers.abstract: Human RNase 2, also named the eosinophil-derived neurotoxin (EDN), is a secretory protein of the vertebrate-specific RNase A superfamily involved in antiviral and proinflammatory cell response. Identifying ligand-binding pockets in EDN is thus relevant to structure-based drug design. By X-ray crystallography we first identified a conserved site at the protein surface binding to carboxylic anion molecules: malonate, tartrate and citrate. Searching for potential biomolecules rich in anion groups and considering previous report of EDN interaction to glycosaminoglycans, we explored the protein bin
papers.summary: This study used X-ray crystallography to identify a conserved surface pocket on human RNase 2/EDN that binds carboxylic anions like malonate, tartrate, and citrate. Building on prior evidence of EDN-glycosaminoglycan interactions, the authors explored saccharide binding, revealing potential lectin-like properties that could inform structure-based drug design targeting this antiviral and proinflammatory protein.

papers.title: Enterovirus 2C Protein Drug Design, Assay Development, and Drug Resistance Studies.
papers.abstract: In this Account, we describe our efforts to establish enteroviral 2C as a tractable target for antiviral drug discovery by integrating medicinal chemistry, molecular pharmacology, resistance profiling, structural modeling, and assay development. Rather than relying solely on conventional phenotypic high-throughput screening, our initial studies focused on the rational optimization of reported 2C inhibitors identified from a drug-repurposing campaign. This strategy led to quinoline-based antivirals with substantially improved potency and selectivity against enterovirus D68 (EV-D68), providing e
papers.summary: This Account describes a multi-disciplinary effort to develop enterovirus 2C protein as a drug target, starting from repurposed hits and using medicinal chemistry to optimize quinoline-based inhibitors with improved potency against EV-D68. The work integrates resistance profiling, structural modeling, and assay development to validate 2C as a tractable antiviral target. It provides a framework for rational antiviral discovery beyond phenotypic screening.

papers.title: From structure prediction to ligand-target recognition: expanding the reach of AlphaFold in natural product research.
papers.abstract: Natural products constitute a structurally diverse reservoir of bioactive molecules and remain an important source of lead compounds for drug discovery. However, the limited availability of structural information on pharmacological targets and biomolecular interactions continues to hinder mechanism elucidation and structure-guided optimization, particularly for complex natural products such as bioactive peptides, proteinaceous natural products, and natural molecular glues. Recent advances in AlphaFold have transformed structural biology by enabling high-confidence prediction of protein structu
papers.summary: This review discusses how AlphaFold's protein structure prediction capabilities are being extended beyond structure determination to ligand-target recognition, addressing the bottleneck of limited structural information on pharmacological targets in natural product research. The authors highlight applications to complex natural products including bioactive peptides, proteinaceous compounds, and molecular glues, where structural data has traditionally been scarce.

papers.title: HEDGEHOG: hierarchical evaluation of drug generators through rigorous filtration.
papers.abstract: Generative molecular models can support early drug discovery by proposing new candidate compounds de novo. In practice, useful candidates must balance target-relevant activity, physicochemical properties, and other multiparameter design constraints. However, standard metrics commonly used to evaluate molecular generators only weakly reflect whether the generated compounds are medicinally plausible and suitable for downstream computation. This can produce an incomplete view of model performance and inefficient use of computational resources. We introduce HEDGEHOG, a configurable six-stage evalu
papers.summary: The authors introduce HEDGEHOG, a configurable six-stage evaluation pipeline for generative molecular models used in drug discovery. It applies hierarchical filtering to assess whether generated compounds are medicinally plausible and suitable for downstream computation, addressing the weak reflection of real-world utility in standard metrics. This provides a more rigorous framework for comparing drug generator performance.

papers.title: Structure-based discovery of novel BCL-XL inhibitors through molecular docking and key interaction-guided virtual screening.
papers.abstract: BCL-XL, an anti-apoptotic member of the BCL-2 protein family, is an attractive therapeutic target for overcoming apoptosis resistance in cancer. However, the large, shallow, and predominantly hydrophobic nature of its BH3-binding groove has complicated the discovery of potent, drug-like small-molecule inhibitors. Here, we employed structure-based virtual screening with key interaction constraints to identify novel BCL-XL inhibitor scaffolds with relatively low molecular weights (MWs). Approximately 312,000 drug-like compounds were docked into the BH3-binding groove, and the top-ranked molecule
papers.summary: This study used structure-based virtual screening of ~312,000 drug-like compounds against the BH3-binding groove of BCL-XL, applying key interaction constraints to find novel low-molecular-weight inhibitor scaffolds. The approach targets a challenging, large and hydrophobic binding site that has historically hindered drug discovery for this anti-apoptotic cancer target.

papers.title: InterPro: the protein sequence classification resource in 2027.
papers.abstract: InterPro (https://www.ebi.ac.uk/interpro) is a freely accessible resource for the classification of protein sequences. It integrates predictive models, known as signatures, from multiple member databases to classify sequences into families and to predict the presence of domains and functionally important sites. The InterPro database provides annotations for hundreds of millions of sequences, ensuring extensive coverage of UniProtKB, the standard repository of protein sequences, and includes mapping to several other major resources, such as Gene Ontology, the Protein Data Bank in Europe (PDBe),
papers.summary: InterPro is a freely accessible database that classifies protein sequences by integrating predictive models (signatures) from multiple member databases to assign proteins to families and identify domains and functional sites. The 2027 update provides annotations for hundreds of millions of sequences, covering UniProtKB extensively and linking to resources like Gene Ontology and PDBe. This makes it a central hub for protein functional annotation and classification.

papers.title: Cytotoxic Activity and Molecular Docking Studies of ONNO Type Salophen Schiff Base Metal Complexes.
papers.abstract: A Schiff base ligand (H2L) was synthesized through the condensation of 3,5-dibromo-2-hydroxybenzaldehyde with 1,2-phenylenediamine and subsequently complexed with Cu(II), Ni(II), Pt(II), Fe(II), and Pd(II) ions. Synthesized compounds were examined using FT-IR, UV-Vis, NMR, mass, elemental analysis, molar conductivity, and magnetic susceptibility. The H2L and transition metal complexes were tested for their cytotoxic activity potential against human liver carcinoma (HepG2) and lung adenocarcinoma (A549) cell lines. The cytotoxic activities of compounds were determined based on their IC50 values
papers.summary: This study synthesized an ONNO-type salophen Schiff base ligand from 3,5-dibromo-2-hydroxybenzaldehyde and 1,2-phenylenediamine, then complexed it with Cu(II), Ni(II), Pt(II), Fe(II), and Pd(II). The ligand and metal complexes were characterized spectroscopically and tested for cytotoxicity against HepG2 liver and A549 lung cancer cell lines, with molecular docking used to rationalize the observed activity. The work reports IC50-based comparisons of the compounds' anticancer potential.

papers.title: A split nozzle and two-protein chain-like fibers define the tail architecture of Pseudomonas aeruginosa podophage A1002.
papers.abstract: Phage therapy offers unique advantages against antibiotic-resistant bacteria. However, high-resolution structural studies of phages targeting Pseudomonas aeruginosa-a top-seven global pathogen-particularly podophages, remain severely limited, directly impeding structure-based development of novel antimicrobials. In this study, we utilize cryo-EM to resolve the high-resolution intact structure of mature phage A1002, a podophage infecting carbapenem-resistant P. aeruginosa. Based on density maps combined with AlphaFold3 predictions, we identified 11 structural protein components from the head to
papers.summary: This study reports the high-resolution cryo-EM structure of podophage A1002, a virus that infects carbapenem-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa. The authors identify 11 structural proteins and describe a unique tail architecture featuring a split nozzle and two-protein chain-like fibers. These structural insights could aid structure-based design of new antimicrobials for phage therapy.

papers.title: PEG10/TRIB3 axis is associated with malignant behavior and Notch-related signaling in oral squamous cell carcinoma cells.
papers.abstract: Oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) is an aggressive oral epithelial neoplasm for which the expression of paternally expressed gene 10 (PEG10) has notable prognostic implications. However, the functional role of this protein in OSCC remains to be fully elucidated. The present study aimed to explore the function of PEG10 in regulating OSCC cell behavior and the potential mechanisms of this regulation. Cell Counting Kit-8, 5-ethynyl-2'-deoxyuridine, wound healing and Transwell assays were employed to estimate cell proliferation, migration and invasion, respectively. Furthermore, flow cytometry a
papers.summary: This study investigates the role of PEG10 in oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) cells, showing that PEG10 expression is linked to malignant behaviors such as proliferation, migration, and invasion. The authors identify a PEG10/TRIB3 axis associated with Notch-related signaling, suggesting a potential mechanistic pathway driving OSCC aggressiveness. The work extends prior prognostic observations of PEG10 to a functional context, though the findings are based on in vitro cell assays.

papers.title: From agricultural waste to functional gels: Mulberry pomace-derived carboxymethyl cellulose synergistically enhances calcium-mediated peanut protein isolate gelation.
papers.abstract: This study aimed to develop a sustainable functional ingredient from mulberry pomace-derived carboxymethyl cellulose (MPCMC) and elucidate its synergistic role with Ca2+ in regulating peanut protein isolate (PPI) gelation. MPCMC was prepared and its effects on PPI gel properties and underlying mechanisms were systematically investigated through multiscale characterization, intermolecular force analysis, correlation analysis, and molecular docking simulation. Results showed that 1.5% MPCMC plus 12 mM Ca2+ increased PPI gel strength from 52.47 g to 142.89 g and water holding capacity from 72.21%
papers.summary: This study extracts carboxymethyl cellulose from mulberry pomace (an agricultural waste stream) and shows that combining it with calcium ions substantially improves the strength and water-holding capacity of peanut protein isolate gels. Multiscale characterization and molecular docking suggest synergistic interactions among the polysaccharide, calcium, and protein drive the improved gel network. The work demonstrates a sustainable route to valorize fruit-processing waste as a functional food ingredient.

papers.title: Identification of Neuroinflammation-Related Diagnostic Biomarkers in Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatohepatitis: An Integrated Bioinformatics and Machine Learning Approach.
papers.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) is a liver disease that progresses and may be connected to neuroinflammation, though the specific molecular mechanisms are not yet understood. The objective of this research was to explore candidate diagnostic biomarkers related to neuroinflammation-associated gene programs for MASH through integrated bioinformatics and machine learning, as a hypothesis-generating study.
papers.summary: This study uses integrated bioinformatics and machine learning to identify candidate diagnostic biomarkers for metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) that are linked to neuroinflammation-related gene programs. The authors frame their work as hypothesis-generating, aiming to uncover molecular connections between liver disease progression and neuroinflammation. The key output is a set of candidate biomarkers rather than validated clinical tools.

papers.title: Carbonic anhydrase 4 restrains dual TLR4-NF-κB/IRF3 innate immune signaling and epithelial-mesenchymal transition in methotrexate-induced pulmonary fibrosis.
papers.abstract: Methotrexate (MTX)-induced pulmonary fibrosis (MTX-PF) is the most severe and frequently irreversible manifestation of MTX pulmonary toxicity, yet the molecular target and signaling circuitry linking drug exposure to fibrosis remain undefined, hampering diagnosis and targeted intervention.
papers.summary: This study identifies carbonic anhydrase 4 (CA4) as a key regulator in methotrexate-induced pulmonary fibrosis. CA4 appears to restrain both TLR4-NF-κB/IRF3 innate immune signaling and epithelial-mesenchymal transition, suggesting that loss of CA4 function contributes to fibrosis progression. The work proposes CA4 as a potential molecular target for diagnosis and intervention in this drug-induced lung toxicity.

papers.title: Comparative multi-target computational profiling of ebelin lactone across cognition-associated proteins.
papers.abstract: Ebelin lactone (EL) is a bacoside-related triterpenoid derivative produced through acid hydrolysis and has previously shown binding affinity toward the M1 muscarinic and 5-HT2A receptors. However, its structural compatibility with proteins involved in synaptic plasticity, neuronal proteostasis, mitochondrial stress responses, and neurite remodeling has not been systematically evaluated.
papers.summary: This study computationally screens ebelin lactone, a plant-derived triterpenoid, against multiple proteins linked to cognition, including those involved in synaptic plasticity, neuronal proteostasis, mitochondrial stress, and neurite remodeling. It extends prior receptor-binding findings by profiling structural compatibility across a broader set of cognition-associated targets. The work is purely computational and provides hypotheses for experimental validation.

papers.title: Integrated pharmacology and validation reveal Formononetin upregulates GSTM2 to modulate prostate cancer immune microenvironment via ROS/STAT3-driven chemokine reprogramming.
papers.abstract: Prostate cancer (PCa) is responsible for a substantial proportion of male cancer cases worldwide. Biochemical recurrence (BCR) representing a critical challenge in its disease management. Formononetin, a natural isoflavone derived from traditional Chinese medicine, has demonstrated potential anticancer properties. We sought to determine the translational potential of Formononetin-targeted molecules in PCa.
papers.summary: This study uses integrated pharmacology and experimental validation to show that the natural isoflavone Formononetin upregulates GSTM2 in prostate cancer cells, which alters ROS/STAT3 signaling and reprograms chemokine expression to modulate the immune microenvironment. The authors propose GSTM2 and downstream chemokine pathways as potential translational targets to address biochemical recurrence in prostate cancer.

papers.title: Mutation-induced structural and dynamic perturbations at the IL-17A-IL-17RA interface: Therapeutic insights from multi-replicate molecular dynamics simulations.
papers.abstract: The interaction between Interleukin-17A (IL-17A) and its receptor IL-17RA plays a key role in pro-inflammatory signal transduction and is implicated in the pathogenesis of inflammatory autoimmune diseases. Blocking this protein-protein interaction is a major approach to developing therapeutic agents to inhibit IL-17A-induced signaling. Predicting the consequences of mutations on structure and function in proteins can be accomplished by using computational methods, which are relatively inexpensive and rapid compared with experimental methods. Here, we used a multidimensional in silico approach
papers.summary: This study uses multi-replicate molecular dynamics simulations to examine how mutations at the IL-17A–IL-17RA protein interface perturb the structure and dynamics of the complex. The authors aim to predict which mutations disrupt binding, offering computational guidance for therapeutic strategies targeting this inflammatory signaling axis. The work is a computational case study rather than an experimental validation.

papers.title: Quercetin ameliorates gestational diabetes mellitus-induced placental dysfunction by modulating the AGE-RAGE-associated oxidative and inflammatory signaling network.
papers.abstract: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) induces placental structural and functional disturbances associated with dysregulated AGE-RAGE/ROS signaling and inflammatory responses. Existing flavonoid-related studies merely observed changes in pathway protein levels, lacking direct experimental proof of molecular binding between candidate compounds and core receptors. This study aimed to investigate the potential involvement of RAGE in the protective effects of quercetin and to characterize the associated AGE-RAGE/ROS/NF-κB-related signaling changes in GDM placental injury.
papers.summary: This study investigates whether quercetin protects against placental dysfunction caused by gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) by targeting the AGE-RAGE signaling pathway. The authors combine experimental evidence of molecular binding between quercetin and RAGE with characterization of downstream ROS and NF-κB inflammatory signaling changes in GDM placental injury models. The work provides direct binding evidence that prior flavonoid studies lacked, supporting quercetin as a candidate therapeutic for GDM-associated placental damage.

papers.title: Kurarinol A from Sophora flavescens suppresses hepatic stellate cell activation via the TLR4/MyD88/NF-κB pathway.
papers.abstract: Sophora flavescens is traditionally used in TCM and Miao/Mongolian/Yi ethnomedicines for hepatobiliary disorders, yet its bioactive flavonoid constituents and mechanisms remain incompletely understood. This study investigated the anti-hepatic fibrosis efficacy, mechanism, and target of the ethyl acetate fraction (EAF) from S. flavescens and its key lavandulyl flavonoid kurarinol A (KA).
papers.summary: This study shows that an ethyl acetate fraction of Sophora flavescens and its flavonoid compound kurarinol A reduce activation of hepatic stellate cells, the key cells driving liver fibrosis, by blocking the TLR4/MyD88/NF-κB inflammatory signaling pathway. The findings support kurarinol A as a candidate natural compound for treating liver fibrosis.

papers.title: SLC5A12 defines an invasive epithelial state associated with immune remodeling and therapeutic vulnerability in HNSCC.
papers.abstract: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) is characterized by marked epithelial and immune heterogeneity. The malignant epithelial states associated with tumor progression, immune remodeling, and potential therapeutic vulnerability remain incompletely defined.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
papers.summary: This study identifies SLC5A12 as a marker of an invasive epithelial cell state in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC), linking this state to immune remodeling within the tumor microenvironment and to a potential therapeutic vulnerability. The work uses transcriptomic profiling to define epithelial heterogeneity and suggests that SLC5A12-high tumors may respond to specific targeted treatments.

papers.title: Integrated machine learning and in vitro pipeline for TRPA1-active chemesthetic flavor compounds: From predictive screening to molecular mechanisms.
papers.abstract: Chemesthesis constitutes a fundamental dimension of food sensory perception, triggered by transient receptor potential ankyrin 1 (TRPA1) ion channels that mediate responses to pungent and irritating flavor compounds. However, efficient prediction of TRPA1 activation by flavor compounds remains limited by the low throughput of traditional experimental screening. Here, we developed an integrated computational and in vitro pipeline to overcome this limitation. Using an optimized Random Forest (RF) machine learning model, we successfully predicted and screened representative flavor compounds. We e
papers.summary: This study combines a Random Forest machine learning model with in vitro experiments to predict and validate flavor compounds that activate the TRPA1 ion channel, which mediates pungent and irritating sensations in food. The pipeline enables higher-throughput screening of chemesthetic compounds than traditional experimental methods alone, and the authors use it to identify representative TRPA1-active flavor compounds and probe their molecular mechanisms.

papers.title: A Tanshinone IIA Sulfonate Derivative Targets USP21 to Induce SCD1 Degradation, Suppressing NSCLC Metabolism and Enhancing Antitumor Immunity.
papers.abstract: Background: The deubiquitinase ubiquitin-specific peptidase 21 (USP21) is a key regulator of tumor metabolism and immune homeostasis in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Its aberrant activation drives malignant growth, metabolic reprogramming and immune resistance, yet specific USP21 inhibitors for NSCLC therapy remain scarce. We aimed to develop a selective USP21 inhibitor, define its immunometabolic mechanism, and validate its anti-tumor and immunotherapy-sensitizing effects in NSCLC. Methods: We performed structure-based hierarchical virtual screening of a Food and Drug Administration (FD
papers.summary: This study identifies a Tanshinone IIA sulfonate derivative as a selective inhibitor of the deubiquitinase USP21 in non-small cell lung cancer. The inhibitor blocks USP21, leading to degradation of the metabolic enzyme SCD1, which disrupts tumor lipid metabolism and enhances antitumor immune responses. The findings suggest a new pharmacological strategy to sensitize NSCLC to immunotherapy.

papers.title: Hupehenine suppresses tumor cell phenotypes and modulates macrophage marker profiles in a diabeticmimetic colorectal cancer model.
papers.abstract: Diabetes is associated with increased colorectal cancer (CRC) risk and mortality, but the molecular links remain incompletely understood. We aimed to characterize shared molecular features of diabetes and CRC, and identify compounds capable of modulating the candidate axis at this interface.
papers.summary: This study identifies shared molecular features between diabetes and colorectal cancer and tests whether the natural compound hupehenine can modulate these pathways. Using a diabetic-mimetic CRC model, the authors show that hupehenine suppresses tumor cell phenotypes and alters macrophage marker profiles, suggesting a potential therapeutic axis at the diabetes–cancer interface.

papers.title: Structure-based minimization of a high-mobility group protein B1 (HMGB1) B box peptide uncouples anti-NETotic activity and anti-biofilm function.
papers.abstract: We previously showed that human HMGB1 has anti-biofilm activity localized to a 97-amino-acid B-Box-derived peptide (mB Box-97), engineered with a C106S mutation to reduce HMGB1's proinflammatory properties while retaining anti-biofilm function. This peptide also suppresses NETosis by inhibiting neutrophil protein kinase C (PKC) activity. Here, we tested whether the anti-biofilm and anti-NETotic activities of mB Box-97 could be separated into distinct shorter peptides by constructing truncated variants containing Helix 1 of the B-Box (with the C106S mutation), with or without the A Box-B Box li
papers.summary: The authors truncated the HMGB1 B-box peptide (mB Box-97) into shorter variants containing Helix 1 to test whether its anti-biofilm and anti-NETosis activities could be separated. They found that these two functions can be uncoupled into distinct shorter peptides, suggesting that the anti-inflammatory (anti-NETotic) and antimicrobial (anti-biofilm) properties of HMGB1 can be engineered independently.
